title: University of Stuttgart Deploys Quantum Dot QKD Link Using Frequency Conversion Over Campus Fiber - Quantum Computing Report
gist: A University of Stuttgart-led team (with Saarland University and Leibniz IFW Dresden) ran entanglement-based BBM92 QKD from a GaAs quantum dot over a 1.59 km deployed campus fiber, using Sagnac frequency conversion to 1515 nm, producing 14.2 Mbit of secure key at 206 Hz secure rate and 4.70% QBER over 19 hours. It positions quantum-dot sources plus frequency conversion as viable transmitters for metropolitan QKD networks.

insights.claim: A University of Stuttgart-led team generated 14.2 Mbit of secure key over a 1.59 km installed campus fiber link using an entanglement-based BBM92 QKD system driven by an epitaxial quantum dot at a 1 GHz excitation rate, and used it for one-time-pad image encryption.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum-dot QKD has moved from lab bench to a deployed (if short) fiber link.
insights.quote: the system generated 14.2 Mbit of secure key material to perform one-time pad image encryption

insights.claim: The Stuttgart quantum-dot QKD link achieved a raw key rate of 504 Hz and a secure key rate of 206 Hz with an average QBER of 4.70%, well below the 11% BBM92 security threshold.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Secure rates in the hundreds of Hz remain far below commercial needs; throughput is the gating metric to watch.
insights.locator: Stuttgart Deployed Quantum Dot QKD Operational Parameters

insights.claim: Automated motorized polarization tracking kept Stokes parameters above 0.995 over 19 hours of continuous operation on the deployed fiber, with throughput dips traced to thermal detuning of a 25 GHz volume Bragg grating filter.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Operational stability over a day is demonstrated; thermal filter control is the identified engineering weak point.
insights.quote: maintained Stokes parameters above 0.995 throughout 19 hours of continuous operation

insights.claim: Error correction and privacy amplification (5,000-bit LDPC blocks plus Toeplitz hashing) retained only 40.87% of raw key, illustrating that post-processing overhead more than halves usable QKD key throughput.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Classical post-processing efficiency is a material lever on effective QKD key rates.
insights.locator: Stuttgart Deployed Quantum Dot QKD Operational Parameters

themes.theme: Why quantum dots vs Poisson sources

insights.claim: Most deployed QKD networks use Poisson-distributed sources (attenuated lasers or SPDC), which face an intrinsic trade-off between brightness and multi-photon emission probability; deterministic sub-Poissonian quantum-dot emission avoids that trade-off.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum-dot sources could eventually lift the brightness ceiling that limits incumbent QKD hardware.
insights.quote: face intrinsic trade-offs between emitter brightness and multi-photon emission probabilities

insights.claim: The main barrier to quantum-dot QKD is wavelength: native GaAs dot emission (779.8 nm) lies outside telecom windows, so a polarization-preserving Sagnac frequency converter was needed to shift photons to 1515 nm in the C-band, at up to 50% internal efficiency.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Frequency-conversion efficiency is a key bottleneck for integrating quantum-dot sources into existing telecom fiber.

insights.claim: The authors conclude that quantum dots paired with frequency conversion are viable transmitters for metropolitan quantum key networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals a possible future source architecture for metro QKD vendors and telecom operators.
insights.quote: The experiment establishes quantum dots paired with frequency conversion as viable transmitters for metropolitan quantum key networks.

insights.claim: Coincidence-window tuning in the Stuttgart system settled at 275 ps: widening the gate captures more photon events but raises error rates from fine-structure precession and conversion noise, a direct rate-versus-QBER trade-off.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows QKD performance is bounded by tunable rate/error trade-offs rather than a single headline number.

insights.claim: The quantum dot's 2.1 μeV fine-structure splitting yielded 91.4% fidelity to the target Bell state within the 275 ps window, sufficient for secure BBM92 operation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Entanglement fidelity of current dot sources is adequate for security but not yet near-ideal.
insights.locator: Stuttgart Deployed Quantum Dot QKD Operational Parameters
